newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura scandal gave push to reform plan--MOF panel.
newsitem.headline: Nomura scandal gave push to reform plan--MOF panel.

text.p: A recent scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd helped push forward proposals for financial reform in Japan, the acting chairman of a Ministry of Finance (MOF) advisory panel told reporters on Friday.
The Securities and Exchange Council earlier on Friday revealed sweeping proposals to reform Japan's securities markets.

"There were no concrete changes to the proposals (as a result of the Nomura case), but as I've said before, the Nomura incident in effect has given a push forward to reform proposals," said Shoichi Royama, acting chairman of the council.

Royama added that the prime minister's tax advisory panel had already begun considering the MOF panel's request that it draft amendments to tax laws, such as those relating to the securities transaction tax, that would be needed to implement its proposed reforms.

Royama also said he strongly hopes that banks will voluntarily unload their shareholdings in companies, such as those related to cross shareholding arrangements, because such holdings give them an undesirable influence over the securities markets.
